title: cost-optimization-autotune-defaults-batching-caching-quant-uecon-tooling
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: We observed that many customers run inference with suboptimal batching and caching defaults and conservative quantization profiles, increasing per-token cost. This PR introduces an autotune path that recommends and applies safe defaults for batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization profiles based on observed workload characteristics and unit-economics tooling. It also surfaces a new UEcon CLI and backend endpoints for estimating per-route cost/latency tradeoffs.

Scope and summary of changes: Adds an autotune service that samples request distributions, infers optimal batch sizes and cache TTLs, and selects a quantization profile (fp16/int8 dynamic/ptq suggestions) subject to quality/regression guards. Adds UEcon tooling (cli + REST endpoint) to simulate per-token cost across candidate configs. Integrates telemetry (new metrics: autotune.suggestions.*, uecon.estimate.*) and console UI hints for suggested configs. Includes unit and integration tests, docs, and rollout feature flag.

Key technical changes: 1) runtime/autotune: new Go service (autotune controller) that aggregates request stats, runs a lightweight optimizer, and emits suggestions. 2) serve/batching: scheduler accepts dynamic batch_size hints and new safe-fallbacks; improved continuous-batching heuristics to reduce tail latency. 3) cache/prefix: KV cache TTL tuning logic plus metric-driven eviction for cross-model sharing. 4) model/quant-profiles: add declarative quant profiles, compatibility matrix, and safety checks; new profile: int8-dyn-fast (good for 7B/13B families). 5) tools/uecon: TS CLI and REST backend to compute unit-econ curves given candidate configs. 6) console: UI hinting and rollout knob.

Safety and regression controls: All suggestions are opt-in by default under the feature flag feature:autotune-defaults. Suggestions include confidence scores and historical A/B results where available. For quantization, we only recommend profiles that passed lightweight quality SIG tests (prompt set regressions < 1% or customer-specified thresholds). Rollout plan: opt-in beta -> staged canary on Dedicated -> default opt-in for newly provisioned workloads after 30 days of stable metrics.

Observed results from internal eval: On a representative corpus of multi-tenant traffic we saw a median 12% reduction in token cost and a 2.5% increase in P99 latency for CPU-backed fallbacks; GPU-backed routes saw 9% cost reduction with <1% latency regression. Unit-econ tooling helped identify 3x different break-even points for int8 vs fp16 across model sizes and sequence lengths.

Migration notes: No forced migrations. Operators can accept suggestions via Console, UEcon CLI, or the new REST endpoint (/v1/autotune/apply). Telemetry tags: autotune.applied=true.

Checklist: - [x] Autotune controller implementation - [x] Batching scheduler integration - [x] KV cache TTL tuning logic - [x] Quant profiles and compatibility checks - [x] UEcon CLI + REST endpoint - [x] Console hinting and rollout flag - [x] Unit/integration tests and CI coverage - [x] Docs: docs/optimize/autotune.md

Related: ENG-4871 (autotune controller), PM-1023 (product requirements), SUP-221 (customer request for cost tooling).
